ownerDecision.request: now make a super modernized hypotehtical version a tier 9 and a tier 10
ownerDecision.scope: Two fictional Brazilian game designs on the surviving Osório P.2 of the 266 Brazil line (profiles/osorio.ts marks t3 and t4): the EE-T3 Osório (tier IX) and the EE-T4 Osório (tier X), continuing Engesa's numbering. No such vehicles were built; their photo packets (docs/references/photos/ee-t3-osorio-concept-20261030.json, ee-t4-osorio-concept-20261030.json) cite the P.2 photographs the base follows.

drums.request: add two big fuel barrels on the backs here
drums.scope: Both marks carry two 200 L fuel drums across the stern (the owner chose the EE-T3 and EE-T4 the same day); the envelopes are re-measured with them.

ee_t3_osorio.silhouette: Fictional Brazilian modernization of the surviving Osório P.2 (tier IX): the P.2's low welded hull and wedge turret under a bolted composite nose module and five composite skirt modules a side, wedge appliqué swept forward of the turret cheeks, three bolted side packs a side, a PERI-pattern commander's panoramic sight, a deeper rear basket with stowage, set-in nose lamps, the 120 mm L/47 in a canvas boot, the roof 7.62 mm, two 200 L fuel drums across the stern in a cradle off the lower rear plate and a three-tone blotch coat.

ee_t4_osorio.silhouette: Fictional Brazilian modernization of the Osório P.2 (tier X), the EE-T3's kit heavier and full length: a nose module carried down a bolted lower-glacis slab with the lamps set in its face, thicker skirt modules, long swept wedges flaring to sharp tips past the mantlet, a bolted block mantlet, thicker side packs, a hard-kill active protection system (four radar panels on the turret corners, two drum launchers on pedestals), laser-warning heads, a slat cage over the rear plate with two 200 L fuel drums in a cradle behind it, the 130 mm L/51 and a three-tone digital coat.
